subject: fix: prevent completions from mutating os.Args via append side effect (#2356)

agent.tail:
I'll start by querying CogZ for relevant context, then look at the code.Let me look at the `getCompletions` function in completions.go.The bug is at line 369: `append(finalArgs, "--")` writes into the shared backing array of `args` (derived from `os.Args`). The fix per the commit description: copy `trimmedArgs` at the top so downstream sub-slices share a private backing array. Let me check the Go version and imports first.Go 1.15 — no `slices` package, so a plain `append` copy is needed. Let me check the test exists and what `Traverse` returns.The test is already in place. Now I'll apply the fix — copy `trimmedArgs` so appends on derived sub-slices can't touch the caller's backing array (`os.Args`).The rule about covering all four shells applies to generator output changes — this fix is in the shared `__complete` path, so it covers all shells at once. Now run the target test.Target test passes. Let me run the full suite to check for regressions.Done. The fix is a one-line change in `getCompletions` at [completions.go:320-323](file:///home/andy/cogz_bench/replay_tmp/cogz_replay_746ef071_x49iiv_q/completions.go).

`trimmedArgs` was a sub-slice of `args` (ultimately `os.Args[1:]`). `Traverse`/`Find` return further sub-slices of it as `finalArgs`, and line 369's `append(finalArgs, "--")` could write `"--"` into the shared backing array when spare capacity existed — corrupting `os.Args`. Copying `trimmedArgs` into a fresh backing array means all downstream appends only touch the private copy.

Verified:
- `go test ./... -run 'TestCompletionDoesNotMutateOsArgs' -count=1` — passes
- `go test ./... -count=1` — full suite passes
